sessionTitle: GitHub Copilot Anywhere: From Remote Control CLIs to Cloud Sandboxes

announcements.name: Cloud Sandboxing for GitHub Copilot in public preview
announcements.shortDescription: Every Copilot session using a cloud sandbox runs in its own isolated cloud environment, with the host machine becoming optional and work persisting even if the local laptop disconnects or shuts down
announcements.longDescription: Cloud sandboxing for GitHub Copilot, now in public preview, gives every Copilot session that uses it its own isolated environment in the cloud, sandboxed down to the tools, file system, and network you choose to grant it. Because the session lives in the cloud, the host machine no longer needs to be running—you can connect even if your laptop disconnects from the internet or shuts down. It also lets users run many heavy agents in parallel by allocating cloud resources instead of overloading local resources.

announcements.name: Remote control sessions for Copilot
announcements.shortDescription: Lets users take a local Copilot session on the go via github.com or the GitHub mobile app, steering and monitoring it in real time across the CLI, the new Copilot desktop app, VS Code, and JetBrains
announcements.longDescription: Remote control sessions let you take a local Copilot session on the go, steering and monitoring work running on your own machine from github.com or a mobile device. The capability applies across clients including the CLI, the new Copilot desktop app launched the prior day, Copilot in VS Code, and Copilot in JetBrains. It also works with any project structure, including GitHub repos, ADO repos, and CLI sessions.

announcements.name: Chronicle session history feature
announcements.shortDescription: Indexes all of a user's Copilot sessions across clients to provide queryable, actionable guidance such as tips, stand-up reports, custom instruction improvements, and cost/token usage reduction
announcements.longDescription: Chronicle builds a queryable history from every Copilot session you run, letting you take actionable steps to improve how you work with Copilot—such as creating stand-up updates, getting tips, and improving custom instructions. It can be run in the desktop app, in the CLI, through VS Code, through JetBrains, and on github.com. Chronicle indexes all of your sessions specific to you across every place you create Copilot sessions.
